course_description:
HLTH1000 (Professions, People and Healthcare) has been designed for students with an interest in working in the Australian health and behavioural sciences sectors.

The multidisciplinary approach to the course delivery will provide students an understanding of the range of roles within Australia's health system and how they contribute to the health and wellbeing of individuals and communities.

Students will have an enhanced capacity to navigate the health landscape in increasingly complex and changing interprofessional collaborative workplaces.

HLTH1000 (Professions, People and Healthcare) has been designed to appeal to students with an interest in working in, or alongside, the Australian health care system. Students learn in an interprofessional and collaborative environment, exploring the organisation and governance of the Australian health system, roles in the health workforce, and concepts of health and health equity as they apply to our population. The course will help prepare graduates for future roles in increasingly complex and changing workplaces, especially those that are interprofessional or multidisciplinary.

restrictions: Faculty of Health, Medicine and Behavioural Sciences undergraduate programs only

Please allocate to
one tutorial
from the available options for each week with timetabled classes (i.e. week 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13).
Each tutorial has limits set by discipline so you may not be allocated a place if your discipline's allocations have been filled. Ensure you have at least three alternatives that you can select from the wide number of options across the week (Monday - Friday, 8am-6pm, 15 tutorial options).
You will attend the same tutorial group each week, and within the tutorial you will be allocated a smaller interprofessional team of 5-6 students. There will be four tutors allocated per session, and each tutor will be the primary point of contact for 5 teams. Tutorial changes after week 3 are discouraged as teams are already forming and completing team agreements.
course_aims: The course aims to introduce first year HMBS students with a foundational learning experience, focussed on perspectives on health, our health system within a global context, healthcare practices and services that are person-centred and collaborative, and health trends and priorities.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify determinants of health, including impacts of social exclusion and marginalisation in Australia.

Describe roles in health and health-related settings in Australia, and priorities to build a resilient, sustainable, distributed and skilled health workforce, including digital health capabilities, health workforce wellbeing and retention.
Explain the structure and organisation of the Australian health care system, including regulation, infrastructure, governance, and funding.

Describe and demonstrate effective collaboration and interprofessional communication in a health context, including emphasising person-centred practices and including people, family, carers and communities as equal participants.
Recognise the different dimensions of cultural safety in health care practice and services, to advance Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples health outcomes.

assessment_details.task_description: Pre-class preparation: Individual Readiness Assurance Tasks (IRAT) or 'pre-class quizzes' The aim of this assessment task is to ensure that students come prepared with a foundational understanding of the course material before engaging in deeper application exercises with their team during tutorials. Students will have approximately five (5) questions or tasks each week. The questions will be in a multiple-choice, single-best-answer format. There will be a formative (practice) IRAT to orientate you to the quiz platform in Week 1. This does not count to the overall IRAT total. There will be 12 summative IRATs in total, spanning weeks 2-13. IRATs will be marked as 0% (not attempted), 1% (minimal effort or incomplete) or 2% (satisfactory level of effort). Each IRAT is worth up to 2% each, to a maximum total of 20%. Your top 10 IRAT results will be counted towards your final grade. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.due_date: 7/10/2026 4:00 pm The patient journey map is due on Wednesday of Week 10, at 4pm. The Peer Assessment Factor is due on Wednesday of Week 11, at 4pm. Follow the information on Blackboard for details of the Peer Assessment Factor and the tutor chat and reflection.

assessment_details.task_description: The Collaborative Assessment consists of three parts with a combined weighting of 30% towards your grade. 1) Patient journey map - the patient journey map is a team assessment task where you illustrate the healthcare journey of ONE of the three key individuals whose journey we follow across the HLTH1000 tutorials. You will explore their interactions with the healthcare system, the healthcare workers involved in their care or service journey, pain points and opportunities for reform. The full task sheet is available on Blackboard. This assessment component contributes up to 15% of your grade, and all team members receive the same mark. 2) Peer assessment factor - Using the UQ Buddy Check software, students will provide a rating and commentary on their own contribution and that of their peers to the team patient journey map task. This assessment component contributes to 7.5% of your grade, and each student receives a unique result based on peer evaluation. 3) Tutor check-in with reflection - you will have TWO (2) brief 1:1 chats with your tutor. The first check in will take place half-way through semester and the second check-in will take place towards the end of semester. These will take place during your allocated tutorial time, where your tutor will check in on your reflections about your engagement with the course, team collaboration and developing cultural safety learning journey - examples of the questions will be made available on Blackboard. The check-in halfway through semester is formative, and the check in towards the end of semester will contribute up to 7.5% of your grade. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing their assessment tasks (excluding the exam). Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
The patient journey map only needs to be submitted by one team member. Submit online via Blackboard Assignments. All students in the team must contribute as agreed in the Team Contract.
If a team member does not contribute to the group assessment task, despite following the steps in the Team Contract, they may be removed from the group and given a score of 0% for this task. Teams must flag non-contribution to their tutor at least two weeks prior to the submission date, to allow appropriate actions to take place in accordance with the Team Contract.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Please ensure you check eligibility for an extension for group assessments.
Ensure you communicate with your tutors and your team throughout to ensure ongoing collaboration and successful completion.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
Patient Journey Map: 10% of the maximum mark (i.e. 10% of 100 = 10 marks) applies every 24-hour period that the assessment is late. This will apply to all team members.
Peer Assessment Factor: no late penalty applies. If you do not complete the peer assessment for your team members by the due date, and you do not have an approved extension, you will receive 0% for this assessment component.
Tutor Check-in: The final check in must occur during the 13-week semester. No extensions are possible. If the check-in does not occur, you will receive 0% for this assessment component.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Online Self Directed Learning Complete the relevant online learning each week prior to your allocated tutorial. Allow ~30 mins and then complete the IRAT (pre-class quiz) prior to class. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 2 - Describing health Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 2 will cover key concepts of definitions of health, measures of health, rights to healthcare in Australia, trends in Australia's health, and the role and goals of a health system. Learning outcomes: L01

Week 3 - Australia's healthcare system Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 3 will cover key concepts of the organisation, governance, and funding of the Australian healthcare system. Learning outcomes: L03

Week 4 - Australia's health workforce Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 4 will cover the key concepts of the composition, roles and regulation of Australia's health workforce, as well as the trends in workforce composition and the wicked problems facing the workforce. Learning outcomes: L02, L03

Week 5 - Determinants of health Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 5 will cover the key concepts of the social, behavioural and biomedical determinants of health, and the impact of determinants on vulnerable and/or marginalised populations in Australia. This will introduce concepts of equity, equality and social justice. Learning outcomes: L01, L05

Week 6 - Cultural Safety in Practice Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 6 covers critical concepts of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories, knowledges and cultures. The online learning contains two Cultural Safety in Practice modules which are core learning for all students in the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Behavioural Sciences. Concepts of cultural awareness and cultural safety are fundamental to the provision of culturally appropriate health care. Learning outcomes: L01, L05

Week 7 - Health literacy Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 7 will explore key concepts of health literacy - both from an individual and organisation level - and person-centred care. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Week 8 - Digital health and technology Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 8 will explore key concepts of technology in healthcare, such as wearable devices, telehealth, e-prescriptions, digital reminders and electronic health records, as well as the emerging use of artificial intelligence in healthcare. Learning outcomes: L02

Week 9 - Mental health and burnout Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 9 will explore very important topics for future health professionals, including recognising mental health challenges in peers, colleagues and self; psychological safety in the workplace; how to report concerns in the workplace; recognising the signs and contributors to burnout; and the impact of mental health and burnout on the sustainability of our health workforce. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Week 10 - Healthcare teams There is no tutorial in week 10, but there is online learning to complete and a pre-class quiz. This quiz should be completed before the week 11 class. Week 10 online learning focuses on teams in healthcare, and the different types and composition of teams. This includes uniprofessional, intraprofessional, multidisciplinary, interprofessional and transprofessional teams. We also look at the way these teams' function, and why it's important. Learning outcomes: L02, L04

Week 11 - Collaborative healthcare settings Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 11 explores real-world examples of collaboration in healthcare settings. These settings include aged care, rehabilitation and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Community Controlled Health Organisations, where collaboration occurs in closer proximity. We'll also look at settings which are highly collaborative, yet practitioners and/or care recipients may not be co-located. We'll analyse what the factors are that makes these teams successful. Learning outcomes: L02, L04, L05

Week 12 - Patient safety and collaborative practice Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 12 explores the intersectionality between enhanced patient safety and effective interprofessional collaborative practice. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04

Week 13 - Wrap up Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial) Week 13 is the final week of HLTH1000. The tutorial will recap all we've learned, engage you in an interactive quiz in the style of your final exam, and involve a celebration with your team and tutorial group, who you've learned alongside this semester. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
